newsitem.title: USA: Lexmark in HP pact, ends patent dispute.
newsitem.headline: Lexmark in HP pact, ends patent dispute.

text.p: Lexmark International Inc said on Monday it agreed with Hewlett-Packard Co to cross-license printer technology, in a deal which resolved a patent infringment dispute between the two.
Lexmark said specific details were confidential, but the companies agreed to cross-license patents filed before a certain date and the deal did not involve royalties.

It said the agreement generally gave the companies a worldwide license to use patents covering the manufacture and sale of printers, as well as accessories and consumable supplies designed for use with each company's own printers.

"Our customers will be the ultimate beneficiaries of this agreement, which gives us important flexibility and freedom in the continuing design and development of leading-edge printing solutions," said Marvin Mann, chairman and chief executive officer. "We are pleased to have resolved this issue to our mutual benefit."
Lexmark said it had nearly 2,000 patents worldwide 100 cross- license agreements of various types with other companies.
